title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.
intro: This training programme equips boards and directors to shape and oversee the firm's culture: setting the tone, measuring behaviour, aligning incentives, holding individuals to account and evidencing sound oversight to regulators.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give directors a practical grounding in how culture drives conduct and customer outcomes, and the governance tools to oversee it. Participants leave able to measure and challenge culture, align incentives and accountability, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: Setting the tone, measuring culture, remuneration and incentives, consumer outcomes, speaking up and whistleblowing, senior manager accountability, conduct MI, misconduct and consequence management, and supervisory focus on culture.
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and members of board risk, audit, remuneration and nomination committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for conduct, people and customer outcomes
Heads of HR, compliance and company secretarial supporting board oversight of culture
Learning Objectives: Explain how culture drives conduct, customer outcomes and misconduct risk
Assess the tone set by the board and senior management and how it is experienced
Evaluate culture measures, conduct MI and the effectiveness of speak-up arrangements
Challenge remuneration and incentive structures that may drive poor behaviour
Apply senior manager accountability and consequence management consistently
Anticipate supervisory scrutiny of culture and agree a board action plan
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the board's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in HR or behavioural science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
FSB, Supplementary Guidance to the FSB Principles and Standards on Sound Compensation Practices (2018)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)

modules.title: Culture and the Board: Setting the Tone
modules.summary: What culture is, why it drives conduct and outcomes, and how the board and senior management set the tone through their own behaviour, decisions and priorities.
objectives: Explain how culture shapes behaviour and conduct risk
Assess the tone from the top, the middle and within teams
Identify the board's own behaviours that reinforce or undermine the desired culture
syllabus: Purpose, values and the culture the firm actually has
Tone from the top, echo from the middle and mood in the team
Board dynamics, groupthink and psychological safety
Case studies of culture failures and the governance lessons

modules.title: Measuring and Monitoring Culture
modules.summary: How boards move from assertion to evidence on culture, using surveys, behavioural indicators and direct observation to form a reliable view.
objectives: Evaluate the indicators and data available on culture
Interpret culture surveys, exit data and behavioural signals critically
Design a board-level culture dashboard
syllabus: Leading and lagging culture indicators
Surveys, focus groups, exit interviews and site visits
Triangulating data: complaints, breaches, audit findings and attrition
A board culture dashboard and how to use it

modules.title: Remuneration and Incentives
modules.summary: How pay, promotion and recognition drive behaviour, how incentive structures have contributed to misconduct, and what the remuneration committee should challenge.
objectives: Explain how financial and non-financial incentives shape behaviour
Challenge incentive structures that reward volume over outcomes
Apply risk adjustment, deferral, malus and clawback effectively
syllabus: Incentive design: balanced scorecards and conduct gateways
Sales incentives and the link to mis-selling
Risk adjustment, deferral, malus and clawback in practice
FSB principles for sound compensation practices

modules.title: Consumer Outcomes and Conduct MI
modules.summary: The board's responsibility for good customer outcomes, how to tell whether products and services deliver them, and the conduct information the board needs.
objectives: Explain the shift from rules-based compliance to outcomes-focused conduct regulation
Specify the conduct MI the board needs on products, pricing, service and complaints
Interpret conduct reports and identify what is missing
syllabus: Fair value, suitability, communications and customer support
Vulnerable customers and differential outcomes
Complaints analysis as a window on culture
Recognising comfort without evidence in conduct reporting

modules.title: Speaking Up and Whistleblowing
modules.summary: Why staff stay silent, how effective speak-up and whistleblowing arrangements work, and how the board gains assurance that concerns are raised, heard and acted on.
objectives: Explain the barriers to speaking up and the conditions that encourage it
Evaluate whistleblowing arrangements, protections and the champion role
Oversee the handling of concerns and protection against retaliation
syllabus: Psychological safety and the cost of silence
Whistleblowing channels, confidentiality and protection
The board whistleblowing champion and reporting to the board
Case studies: ignored warnings and their consequences

modules.title: Senior Manager Accountability
modules.summary: How senior manager accountability regimes allocate individual responsibility, how the board uses them to drive conduct, and what reasonable steps look like in practice.
objectives: Explain the core features of senior manager accountability regimes
Evaluate statements of responsibilities, mapping and conduct rule training
Apply the reasonable steps standard to board and executive oversight
syllabus: Statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps
Conduct rules for directors, senior managers and staff
Certification and annual fitness and propriety assessment
Evidencing reasonable steps and handling accountability gaps

modules.title: Misconduct and Consequence Management
modules.summary: How the firm identifies, investigates and responds to misconduct, and how consistent consequences reinforce the culture the board wants.
objectives: Assess the firm's processes for identifying and investigating misconduct
Evaluate whether consequences are applied consistently, regardless of seniority or performance
Oversee regulatory references, notifications and remediation
syllabus: Breach and misconduct reporting and root cause analysis
Fair and consistent investigations and disciplinary outcomes
Star performers, double standards and the message they send
Regulatory references, notifications and lessons learned

modules.title: Supervisory Focus on Culture and Board Action Plan
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining how supervisors assess culture and governance, and agreeing a board action plan for culture, conduct and accountability.
objectives: Explain how supervisors assess culture, behaviour and governance
Prepare the board to evidence its oversight of culture to supervisors
Produce a board action plan for culture, conduct and accountability
syllabus: Supervisory approaches to culture: drivers, indicators and reviews
International work on culture and misconduct risk, including FSB guidance
Board self-assessment of culture oversight
Workshop: the board's twelve-month culture and conduct plan

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.

related.title: Induction for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: A ten-module induction giving new directors of regulated firms the grounding to discharge their duties, understand supervisory expectations and oversee the firm's risks.
